internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: directed dispatch from a sender toward a recipient, normally carrying an entrusted message, task, sign, or effect
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All 513 occurrences belong to sending, a sent messenger, or the entrusted communication carried by dispatch. Sender, recipient, payload, and mission vary, while directed commissioning remains.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Form IV supplies caused dispatch; agent nouns profile the one dispatched; underived nouns lexicalize messenger or message. Participants and complements supply source, destination, and payload.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: Natural effects such as winds or punishment can be sent without a speaking messenger, so the core must be dispatch rather than human message-bearing.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The root means messenger alone; 130 sending verbs and non-person payloads refute that restriction.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from bringing and giving because rsl encodes a sender-originated trajectory or commission toward a recipient.
internal_discovery.rationale: A directed-dispatch relation is recurrent, distinctive, and universal across the largest Wave 2 packet.
